correctness.rationale: The crown graph has diameter three, and every forbidden three-edge geodesic is a_i-b_j-a_k-b_i for pairwise distinct indices. Under a_i b_j <-> i -> j these triples are exactly the transitive directed triangles. For each arc u -> v in a transitive-triangle-free digraph, N+(u) and N+(v) are disjoint and N-(u) and N-(v) are disjoint. Summing the two endpoint-degree inequalities over all arcs yields sum_x(d+(x)+d-(x))^2 <= 2mn; Cauchy--Schwarz gives 4m^2/n <= 2mn and hence m <= n^2/2. The balanced bidirected cut is transitive-triangle-free and has floor(n^2/2) arcs. The standalone checker exhaustively verifies n=3,4,5.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact all-n value on a standard dense regular bipartite family specifically within a bipartite direction highlighted by the foundational source. It converts the graph-geodesic problem into a transparent directed extremal problem and proves a sharp quadratic law. The result unifies two previously known isolated special cases without relying on them for the general proof.
